topics.label: Introduction and Course Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, outlines the course structure and learning outcomes, and previews the core themes of cancer biology.

topics.label: Cancer as a Failure of Differentiation and Tissue Organization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish that cancer results from accumulated genetic alterations disrupting normal developmental differentiation and tissue architecture, and discuss how this biology is modeled in culture.

topics.label: Benign Versus Malignant Tumors: Invasion, Progression, and Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the distinctions between benign and malignant neoplasms through their invasive behavior, metastatic spread, histological progression, and standardized naming conventions.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Disease, Mortality, and Comparative Cancer Incidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors physiologically cause illness and death, alongside the patterns of cancer incidence and mortality observed in human populations and across animal species.

topics.label: Principles and Methods of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical rationale, histological foundations, and practical limitations of screening programs for detecting early and pre-invasive tumors.

topics.label: Conclusion and Practical Session Preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by reiterating the learning outcomes and previewing the upcoming practical sessions.
